```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

peabiru computes travel times and accessibility on transport networks built
from an [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org) extract and
[GTFS](https://gtfs.org) public transport feeds, by walking, cycling, driving
and public transport. The routing engine is written in Rust and runs inside
the R session: no Java is needed, and the network is built once, in memory.
If you know r5r, the functions and arguments will look familiar; the article
"Coming from r5r" on the package website lists what carries over.

This vignette runs on the small network that ships with the package: the
streets around Avenida Paulista in São Paulo, the city's frequency-based bus
and metro feed, and 27 points of a hexagonal grid. Every chunk below runs in
a fraction of a second.

```{r}
library(peabiru)
```

## Build a network

A network is built from a directory holding one `.pbf` file and any number of
GTFS `.zip` files. It lives in memory and is reused by every routing call.

```{r}
data_path <- system.file("extdata/spo", package = "peabiru")
list.files(data_path)

network <- build_network(data_path, n_threads = 2)
network
```

Points are a `data.frame` with `id`, `lon` and `lat` (or a `POINT` `sf`
object with an `id` column). Here the points also carry opportunity counts,
used for accessibility below.

```{r}
points <- read.csv(file.path(data_path, "spo_points.csv"))
head(points)
```

## Travel times on the street network

`travel_time_matrix()` with one street mode gives the travel time in whole
minutes from every origin to every destination; pairs that cannot be reached
within `max_trip_duration` (120 minutes by default) are left out.

```{r}
walk <- travel_time_matrix(network, points, points, mode = "WALK",
                           n_threads = 2)
head(walk)

bike <- travel_time_matrix(network, points, points, mode = "BICYCLE",
                           n_threads = 2)
car <- travel_time_matrix(network, points, points, mode = "CAR",
                          n_threads = 2)
sapply(list(walk = walk, bike = bike, car = car),
       function(m) mean(m$travel_time_p50))
```

Walking is at `walk_speed` (3.6 km/h by default). Cycling is at `bike_speed`
on streets whose level of traffic stress is at most `max_lts`; elsewhere the
cyclist walks the bike. Driving uses each street's speed, turn costs and turn
restrictions.

## Travel times by public transport

With `mode = c("WALK", "TRANSIT")` the trip combines walking and public
transport. A departure time is needed, and the result summarises the trips
that leave in each minute of `time_window` as percentiles. This feed is
frequency-based, so the departures are simulated with random draws: give a
`seed` to make them reproducible.

```{r}
departure <- as.POSIXct("2019-05-13 14:00:00", tz = "America/Sao_Paulo")

ttm <- travel_time_matrix(
  network, points, points,
  mode = c("WALK", "TRANSIT"),
  departure_datetime = departure,
  time_window = 10,
  percentiles = c(25, 50, 75),
  seed = 42,
  n_threads = 2
)
head(ttm)
```

Walking all the way is one of the options considered, so here adding public
transport never makes a trip longer; on this small network it shortens many of
the longer ones:

```{r, fig.width = 5, fig.height = 4.2, fig.alt = "Scatter plot of the median travel time by walking and public transport against the walking time, for every pair of points: all points are on or below the diagonal."}
both <- merge(walk, ttm, by = c("from_id", "to_id"),
              suffixes = c("_walk", "_transit"))
mean(both$travel_time_p50_transit < both$travel_time_p50_walk)

plot(both$travel_time_p50_walk, both$travel_time_p50_transit,
     xlab = "walking (min)", ylab = "walk + transit, median (min)",
     pch = 16, col = "#b4532a80", asp = 1)
abline(0, 1, col = "grey50")
```

## Accessibility

`accessibility()` counts the opportunities each origin can reach. With the
`"step"` function and two cutoffs, the result is the number of jobs within
15 and within 30 minutes:

```{r}
access <- accessibility(
  network, points, points,
  opportunities_colnames = "jobs",
  mode = c("WALK", "TRANSIT"),
  departure_datetime = departure,
  decay_function = "step",
  cutoffs = c(15, 30),
  seed = 42,
  n_threads = 2
)
head(access)
```

The other decay functions (`"exponential"`, `"fixed_exponential"`,
`"linear"` and `"logistic"`) weight opportunities by travel time instead of
counting them.

## Trip by trip

`expanded_travel_time_matrix()` keeps every trip instead of a percentile:
one row per departure minute and, with a frequency-based feed, per draw.
With `breakdown = TRUE` each trip is split into its access walk, waiting,
riding, transfers and egress walk, with the routes taken.

```{r}
trips <- expanded_travel_time_matrix(
  network, points[1, ], points,
  mode = c("WALK", "TRANSIT"),
  departure_datetime = departure,
  time_window = 2,
  breakdown = TRUE,
  seed = 42,
  n_threads = 2
)
subset(trips, to_id == "89a8100c02fffff")
```

`arrival_travel_time_matrix()` answers the reverse question: for each pair,
the latest departure that still arrives by a given time.

## Writing results to files

For matrices too large to hold in memory, `output_dir` (an existing
directory) makes each of these functions write its result there, as r5r
does, instead of returning it: one CSV file per origin, `from_<id>.csv`,
byte for byte the file r5r writes for the same call. The origins are routed
a slice at a time, and the function returns `output_dir`.

```{r}
out <- tempfile("peabiru-")
dir.create(out)
travel_time_matrix(network, points, points, mode = "CAR", n_threads = 2,
                   output_dir = out) == out
length(list.files(out))
head(read.csv(file.path(out, list.files(out)[1])), 3)
```

## What is not supported yet

Options that peabiru does not implement yet stop with an error rather than
being ignored: fares, congestion and traffic-stress scenarios and elevation.
For example:

```{r, error = TRUE}
travel_time_matrix(network, points, points, mode = "CAR",
                   carspeed_scale = 0.5)
```

The help pages of `travel_time_matrix()`, `accessibility()`,
`expanded_travel_time_matrix()` and `arrival_travel_time_matrix()` list each
argument and its default.
